text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 432:
Breast-wheel. This holds intermediate place between overshot and undershot wheels; has float-boards like the former, but the cavities between are converted into buckets by moving in a channel adapted to circumference and width, and into which water enters nearly at the level of axle.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 432; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_432.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 434:
In the center are a number of fixed curved “shutes” or guides, A, which direct the water against the buckets of the outer wheel, B, which revolves, and the water discharges at the circumference.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 434; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_434.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 435:
The guides, a, are outside, and the wheel, b, revolves within them, discharging the water at the center.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 435; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_435.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 436:
The “shutes” are arranged on the outside of a drum, radial to a common center and stationary within the trunk or casing, b. The wheel, c, is made in nearly the same way; the buckets exceed in number those of the shutes, and are set at a slight tangent instead of radially, and the curve generally used is that of the cycloid or parabola.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 436; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_436.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 437:
Volute wheel, having radial vanes, a, against which the water impinges and carries the wheel around. The scroll or volute casing, b, confines the water in such a manner that it acts against the vanes all around the wheel. By the addition of the inclined buckets, c, c, at the bottom, the water is made to act with additional force as it escapes through the openings of said buckets.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 437; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_437.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 438:
Barker’s or reaction mill. Rotary motion of central hollow shaft is obtained by the reaction of the water escaping at the ends of its arms, the rotation being in a direction the reverse of the escape.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 438; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_438.html.
